title: Directed colimits of faithfully flat algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, and let $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of commutative $R$-algebras with $R$-algebra transition maps and colimit $S=\varinjlim_i S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If each structural map $R\to S_i$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], then $R\to S$ is faithfully flat. No injectivity or faithful flatness of the transition maps is assumed.

proof.text: View each S_i as an R-module. Since R to S_i is faithfully flat, it is flat. The underlying R-module S is the filtered colimit of the underlying modules S_i, so the existing filtered-colimit flatness lemma gives that S is flat over R.

source.place: Tag 090N, proof first sentence citing Lemma 05UT (lemma-colimit-flat), lines 9285-9289

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal m of R. For every i, the new maximal-ideal nonvanishing lemma gives S_i/mS_i nonzero from faithful flatness of R to S_i. Apply the tensor-colimit statement to the R-module R/mR: the colimit of the modules S_i tensor_R R/mR, identified with S_i/mS_i, is S tensor_R R/mR, identified with S/mS. The transition maps are unital algebra maps, so the class of 1 in this colimit cannot be zero: if it became zero at a later stage, the image of 1 there would be zero, contradicting that every S_j/mS_j is nonzero. Hence S/mS is nonzero for every maximal m.

source.place: Tag 090N, proof middle sentences citing Lemma 00HP and the identification S/mS = colim S_i/mS_i, lines 9290-9298

proof.text: The flat map R to S has S/mS nonzero for every maximal ideal m, so the flat-module faithful-flatness criterion applies and proves that R to S is faithfully flat.
